items.claim: A permissive sudoers entry, a world-writable service unit, or an over-permissive file permission yields root without any kernel or software vulnerability.
items.body:
In practice on HTB this shows up as: | `sudo -l` | Can the user run anything as another user? |
| `ls -la /etc/cron.daily` | Check for daily Cron jobs |
| `lsblk` | Check for unmounted file systems/drives |
| `find / -path /proc -prune -o -type d -perm -o+w 2>/dev/null` | Find world-writeable directories |

Write-up provenance: Esther7171/HackTheBox-Writeups-Walkthroughs :: Write-ups/Academy/06. Post-Exploitation/32. Linux Privilege Escalation/Linux Privilege Escalation.md (490 words, classified network).
items.disproof: Refuted when the permission model forbids the escalation -- no unsafe sudoers entry, no writable unit or script the service runs, and no permissive capabilities -- leaving no configuration path to root.
